AI-GENERATED DRAFT — PENDING HUMAN FACT-CHECK. Not for publication without review.

Independence of Consciousness: Non-Local Mind Models and Reported Perceptual Anomalies

Project Parallax — research draft (not a final publication). This text uses only the supplied dataset. No additional figures have been added.

Scope and evidential limits

This draft treats “independence of consciousness” and “non-local mind” as open research questions, not as established findings. The supplied packet is labeled an illustrative model. Several fields are explicitly incomplete. A human must add a specific study and its reported figure before any quantitative claim about perceptual recall or veridical anomaly can be published.

A previous version of this model hardcoded an uncited number in the perceptual-recall position. That figure has been removed. No replacement value is present in the dataset (perceptual_recall_score is empty). In line with the skeptic critique below, no recall percentage, hit rate, or similar statistic is stated here as fact.

Related source material on disorders of consciousness

An arXiv-related source flag is present in the dataset (arxiv_source_found is true). The supplied abstract fragment concerns prognostication in chronic disorders of consciousness, not a direct test of non-local mind models. It should not be read as settling claims about independent or non-local consciousness.

Prognostication of chronic disorders of consciousness using brain functional networks and clinical characteristics. Disorders of consciousness are a heterogeneous mixture of different diseases or injuries. Although some indicators and models have been proposed for prognostication, any single method when used alone carries a high risk of false prediction. This study aimed to develop a multidomain pr[fragment ends]

As reported in that fragment, disorders of consciousness are described as heterogeneous, and single-method prognostication is described as carrying a high risk of false prediction. The stated aim is to develop a multidomain approach; the supplied text is truncated and does not include methods, results, or outcome figures. Those results are therefore not summarized here.

That clinical-prognostication context is adjacent to questions about residual awareness, but it is not, on the text provided, a source for non-local or extra-bodily perception claims. Linking the two would require human-sourced citation beyond this packet.

Listed electrophysiological ranges (not interpreted as proof of non-locality)

The dataset lists an isoelectric EEG duration literature range of 10–30 seconds. This is recorded as a literature-range field only. This draft does not treat that range as evidence that consciousness is independent of the brain, nor as a measured result from a named experiment in this packet.

Auditory evoked potential status is labeled in the dataset as typically absent per literature. That label is reproduced below as supplied. It is not used here to argue for or against preserved, independent, or non-local awareness.

Reported perceptual anomalies and citation boundary

Subjective reports of perceptual anomalies are sometimes discussed in connection with non-local mind models. Confirming that such reports are veridical (accurate with respect to independent events) is a methodological problem, not a default assumption. The dataset marks boundary_status as requiring a human-sourced citation. No perceptual recall score is supplied.

Accordingly, this draft does not attach a numeric accuracy, correlation, or “hit” value to anomaly reports. Language such as “proves,” “confirms,” or “demonstrates conclusively” is avoided because the packet does not contain a citable method that would support it.

Working synthesis for human review

What can be said from this packet alone is limited. A related arXiv fragment discusses multidomain prognostication in heterogeneous disorders of consciousness and warns that isolated indicators risk false prediction. Separate literature-range labels give an isoelectric EEG window of 10–30 seconds and state that auditory evoked potentials are typically absent. Those items are consistent with a clinical-electrophysiology discussion; they are not, as supplied, a test of non-local mind.

What cannot be said: that consciousness has been shown to operate independently of the brain; that reported perceptual anomalies are veridical; or that any recall score (including any previously hardcoded placeholder) is a publishable result. The skeptic critique is aligned with the empty recall field and the citation boundary: without a specific, citable study and method, no such figure or claim is publishable as fact.

Items required before any later version

  • A human-sourced bibliographic citation for any anomaly or non-local claim, including methods used to assess veridicality.
  • Replacement of the empty perceptual recall field only with a figure that appears in that cited study, attributed as “the study reports.”
  • No reuse of the removed uncited placeholder as if it were data.
  • If the arXiv fragment is used, a complete bibliographic record and the missing remainder of the abstract or paper, so that prognostic results are not guessed from a truncated line.
